subject: PaperTrail AI — dedicated-capacity intake & traffic snapshot
messages:
From: Samantha Reyes <samantha@papertrail.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Daniel Cho <daniel@papertrail.ai>
Date: Fri, 27 Apr 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: PaperTrail AI — dedicated capacity discussion

Hi Laura / Karthik,

Thanks for the call earlier — Daniel and I put together a short snapshot of our expected production profile and want to confirm what you need from us to get a conservative reserved-capacity quote. At a minimum we can share sample traffic traces and a prompt set.

High level: we run an agent platform that fans out model calls across sessions. Our product team expects production rollout in Q3 and is asking for a committed plan with cost guidance.

Could you send your pre-sales sizing questionnaire? We can fill it and also share an anonymized trace.

Thanks,
Samantha
Samantha Reyes
Head of Infrastructure, PaperTrail AI
Samantha@papertrail.ai

Attachment: papertrail_traffic_sample.json (preview)
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 27 Apr 2028 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: PaperTrail AI — dedicated capacity discussion

Hi Samantha — great talking with you.

Attaching our dedicated sizing worksheet (redwood_dedicated_sizing_questionnaire.xlsx). To make our initial capacity sketch accurate, please fill out the shaded sections but the most helpful fields are:
- steady-state RPS and p95/p99 latency requirements
- expected burst factors and burst window length (seconds/minutes)
- prompt / response token distribution (median, 75th, 95th) and any long-tail prompt examples
- percent of requests requiring full generation vs embeddings vs reranking
- whether you need session affinity (sticky KV cache) or truly stateless requests
- top model families you expect to serve (open LLM name or comparable perf profile)
- expected retention / KV cache TTL and cold-start behavior for session reconstructions

If you prefer, you can paste a sample 24h trace (timestamps + latency + input_tokens + output_tokens + model) and we'll synthesize a sizing runbook.

I also dropped a quick checklist for security / compliance items we might need if this moves to Dedicated Reserved: SOC2 scope, VPC peering, KMS requirements.

Next steps: once we have the questionnaire back we can run a cost/throughput estimate and lock in a time for a capacity workshop. If helpful, here's a short calendar link to book a 60-min sizing workshop: https://cal.redwood.ai/laura-bennett/60.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.ai

Attachment: redwood_dedicated_sizing_questionnaire.xlsx

Laura — quick note, flag that PaperTrail said their product is agent-based (session affinity likely). If they want sticky KV cache across requests, we should consider recommending shard-local sessions (reduce KV egress). Also check whether they plan to quantize models — that changes GPU per-TPS significantly.

Subject: Re: PaperTrail AI — dedicated capacity discussion

Laura / Marissa — thanks, attached is a sanitized 24h trace and a short answers doc (papertrail_traffic_sample.json). Quick answers inline below to speed the workshop scheduling: 

- Steady-state: ~200 RPS across our US region (global distribution later).
- Bursts: up to 2,000 RPS for short windows (~90–180s), triggered by product events.
- Latency SLOs: soft p95 <= 350ms, p99 <= 900ms for interactive routes; background jobs can be higher.
- Token mix: median prompt 120 tokens, median response 320 tokens; 90th percentile response ~1,100 tokens (rare long-tail).
- Request types: ~92% generation, ~6% embeddings, ~2% reranking.
- Session affinity: yes — we maintain session state and would benefit from sticky KV caching. Estimated average session TTL ~12 minutes.
- Models: primarily open Llama3-70B / Llama3-13B variants and a small subset of optimized quantized weights. We'll flag any model swaps in the questionnaire.
- Retention: we retain short-term session KV for 12 minutes; persistent logs are stored for 30 days.

We've attached: papertrail_traffic_sample.json (anonymized sample), example_prompt_set.txt (10 representative prompts). Let us know if you need more granularity (per-route breakdown).

Regards,
Daniel Cho
Platform Engineering, PaperTrail AI

Attachment: papertrail_traffic_sample.json, example_prompt_set.txt
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Daniel Cho <daniel@papertrail.ai>, Samantha Reyes <samantha@papertrail.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 28 Apr 2028 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: PaperTrail AI — dedicated capacity discussion

Thanks Daniel — received and very helpful. Initial read on their profile: sticky sessions + long-tail responses push for higher KV-cache memory and local session pinning. Given the 2k short burst and p99 objective, preliminary options to discuss in the workshop:

- Start with a 8-GPU reserved pool (mix of 4x larger-weights and 4x accelerator-optimized instances) to cover steady-state + short bursts with autoscale headroom; final GPU count depends on quantization and exact model choices.
- Recommend enabling prefix/KV caching with per-session pinning to reduce repeated attention-compute for agents; TTL aligned with your 12-minute average session is reasonable.
- Plan a 60-min capacity workshop to synthesize sizing runs from your trace and produce a provisional reserve+burst plan and cost estimate.

Please book here for the workshop: https://cal.redwood.ai/laura-bennett/60 or suggest a time next week. We'll prepare an initial provisional estimate ahead of the call so you have something to circulate to procurement.

I'll also loop in our model-performance engineer if you want us to baseline Llama3-70B vs quantized 13B for a cost/latency comparison.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.ai
